hook: FBI HQ case file 62-HQ-83894, Sub-file A: a compiled dossier of newspaper clippings, routing slips, and investigative case references spanning July 1947 through at least June 1960, tracking public UFO reports and researcher activity as they crossed the FBI's desk.
why_it_matters: This sub-file reveals that the FBI was systematically clipping and routing UFO news coverage to senior leadership—including Associate Director Tolson and multiple Assistant Directors—indicating institutional attention at the highest levels, not merely field-office curiosity. The file captures the full arc of the early UFO era: from the first Washington DC sightings in July 1947 to Carl Jung's 1958 public statement that UFOs 'show signs of intelligent guidance by quasi-human pilots,' to a 1960 photographic evidence dispute where a civilian photographer alleged the Pentagon degraded his color slide before returning it. The inclusion of APRO (Aerial Phenomena Research Organization) materials and Mrs. Lorenzen's name signals FBI awareness of organized civilian UFO research networks.
key_findings: In July 1947, two women on Minnesota Avenue NE in Washington DC reported three golden, dish-shaped objects moving at jet speed—one of the earliest DC sightings in the file, routed to the FBI's highest leadership.

Carl Jung issued a public statement (released July 29 through APRO at Holloman Air Force Base) asserting UFOs are real, 'do not behave in accordance with physical laws,' and show 'signs of intelligent guidance by quasi-human pilots,' with research dating back to 1944.

Joe Perry of Grand Blanc, Michigan (FBI case 65-2477-105) photographed a saucer-like object silhouetted against the full moon; after the FBI and Air Force examined his color slide, the Pentagon returned it claiming 'faulty development'—Perry alleged the image had visibly faded and was no longer the same.

A APRO-reported mass sighting involved nine witnesses who observed a group of unidentified objects hovering for over an hour, which then 'broke apart and reappeared'; military bases, airports, and U.S. Weather Service confirmed no jets or weather balloons in the area during the 8:40–11:30 PM window.

Air Technical Intelligence Center at Wright-Patterson stated its investigators found zero physical evidence—no landing impressions, footprints, or hardware—across 5,700 reported sightings investigated between 1947 and 1957, while Science Service simultaneously noted some sightings came from 'reliable observers accustomed to looking at the sky.'

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: The Air Technical Intelligence Center's 5,700-sighting investigation record cited in this file is the operational core of what became Project Blue Book, and the file explicitly references ATIC's conclusions and methodology.
Wright-Patterson Air Force Base is named as the home of the Air Technical Intelligence Center whose investigators responded to sightings like the Kearney, Nebraska landing report.
The systematic FBI routing of UFO press clippings to senior leadership mirrors contemporaneous CIA interest in monitoring public and media UFO discourse during the same 1947–1960 period.
